name: Aster Channels
description: A Channels page in the Jellyfin dashboard for Aster Media Player. A channel is a video playlist tagged aster:channel, its settings more aster: tags on the same playlist; this page reads and writes those tags exactly as the app does, so the app, the page and tagging by hand all edit the same channels. It also keeps groups for Jellyfin's Live TV channels, which Aster's guide follows.
overview: Make and edit Aster Media Player's TV channels from the dashboard.

versions.changelog:
- 0.2.0.0: Channel groups. A Group box for each channel (aster:group=), shown in the channel list; and a Live TV
  Groups section that puts Jellyfin's Live TV channels into groups for Aster's guide and channel flicking.
- 0.1.1.0: A "?" beside every setting explains it in plain words: hover over it, tab to it or tap it. - 0.1.0.0: First release. A Channels page in the dashboard: the channel list, drag to renumber, a Basic and
  Advanced editor for every setting, and New Channel from a show, genre, network, collection or playlist.

name: Aster Disc
description: Loads user-authored disc menu definitions (schema/menu.schema.json), resolves them against a local, never-shared binding file (schema/binding.schema.json), and exposes the matched entries as the parent item's Special Features. Developed primarily with an AI coding assistant (Claude Code) and not independently reviewed by a human: see the README before relying on it.
overview: User-authored, shareable disc menus for Jellyfin special features.

versions.changelog:
- 0.7.4.0: Disc menus follow each user's library access and parental controls: a title a profile can't see has no menu for
  it, and extras, trailers and theme songs it can't see are left out of the menus it can. API keys are unaffected.
- 0.7.3.0: The Disc Menu button appears on a title you reach by clicking, without reloading the page. The web client moves
  between pages without loading a new one, and the plugin only noticed when the page was loaded or the address was typed;
  it now follows the web client's own navigation, and the button moves with you from one title to the next.
- 0.7.2.0: Security fix. An endpoint that needed no sign-in (the callback for the optional File Transformation plugin) sent
  back whatever page it was sent, on the server's own address, so a malicious website could run script as a signed-in user,
  an administrator included, and take over their session. The endpoint is removed. Nothing else changes: the plugin already adds
  its script to the web client itself, with or without File Transformation. Update as soon as you can.
- 0.7.1.0: A series with no menu of its own now shows its season's menu, and its Disc Menu button, when exactly one of
  its seasons has a menu. A one-season anime under Shokofin, whose menu is matched to the season by AniDB id, no longer
  hides its button on a season page people rarely open (Aster Aurora's Episodes row keeps them on the series page).
  Play still plays the season. The menu document now says which item it is for (ItemId).
- 0.7.0.0: Menus can be matched by AniDB id, so anime libraries managed by Shoko/Shokofin can have disc menus. A
  movie or series is matched by its AniDB id like any other id; a season menu with an AniDB id is matched to the
  season whose own AniDB entry it is, so its seasonNumber is optional (and only breaks ties) however Shoko
  numbers the seasons. "New..." in the Menu Editor makes an AniDB-matched menu for a title that has only an
  AniDB id. Existing menus match exactly as before.
- 0.6.0.0: Disc Menus is now Aster Disc, one of the Aster companion plugins, installed from github.com/peppy6582/aster-companion-plugins. It updates in place: on first start it moves its settings and data (menus, bindings, catalogue, assets) across from the old name. Nothing else changes; its API paths stay the same. - 0.5.0.0: Arrange on the preview: click a button, the title or a decoration in the Menu Editor's preview, drag it
  into place (snapping to a grid and the centre lines), resize layers with a handle, nudge with the arrow keys,
  and undo it in one step; pages that lay their buttons out themselves can be switched to free placement. The
  plugin no longer needs the File Transformation plugin: it adds its own button to the web client (right after
  Play) and works with a configured base URL. Fixes: the preview no longer pulls the cursor out of a form field
  while you type.
- 0.4.1.0: Menu Editor: upload pictures and sounds for a menu and choose them from a panel (checked for type,
  contents and size; uploaded files are public like all menu assets), and pick a title's TMDB backdrops from
  a list. The Disc Menu button now sits in the item page's own button row, right after Play.
- 0.4.0.0: A new Menu Editor: choose a page or button from a list and change it in a form (the raw text is
  optional, behind Show text), with only the essentials shown and the rest under More options. Problems say
  which part they are about and clicking one selects it. Add, move and remove buttons, pages, extras and
  decorative layers, with Undo and Redo. Backups made in the same moment no longer overwrite each other.
- 0.3.0.0: Menu Editor: create a menu for a title in your library, duplicate or delete a menu, and list and
  restore earlier saved versions. Editing from the editor now changes the text in place, so formatting is
  kept and undo works step by step. A key repeated within one menu is now an error instead of silently
  using the last one.
- 0.2.0.0: A Menu Catalogue page in the dashboard to browse, install, update and remove menus from the
  community catalogue (your library is never sent anywhere; every menu is checked against a published
  fingerprint). fanart.tv backgrounds, looked up and served by your own server with your own API key, and a
  fanart.tv picker in the Menu Editor. The settings page gains a write-only fanart.tv key with a test button.
- 0.1.0.0: Early alpha. Shareable disc menus with layouts, backgrounds, music, transitions and scene
  selection; automatic matching to library titles; a dashboard menu editor with live preview.

name: Aster OP-ED
description: Put opening and ending theme files (video, audio or both) in a folder, one folder per show. The plugin matches them to your shows and seasons, adds song title, artists and episode ranges from AnimeThemes.moe, and serves them to clients through an authenticated API. Missing a theme? It can cut one out of your own episodes from their chapter markers, for you to review. Developed primarily with an AI coding assistant (Claude Code); see the README.
overview: Anime openings and endings for your shows, matched from a folder you fill.

versions.changelog:
- 0.5.0.0: Music videos. Put the song's music video beside a theme as OP1-MV (or OP1 (Music Video), OP1 [MV], OP1 - MV - Artist, OP1 - Song (MV) - Artist) and it's kept with OP1, like a full version: made playable, published as "Song (Music Video)" in the Music Videos library and its sound as another song in the Music library, and offered to clients (HasMusicVideo, MvVideoMp4Url, MvAudioM4aUrl, the music video's items). A clash names both ways to tell versions apart. Both libraries are republished once by themselves.
- 0.4.1.0: Full versions can be named the way people write them: OP1 Full, OP1 (Full), OP1 [Full Version], OP1 - Full - Eve, or OP1 - Kaikai Kitan (Full) - Eve, as well as OP1-Full. Before, "OP1 - Full - Eve" was read as a song called "Full", and the file taken for a second copy of OP1. Two files for the same place are now listed in the scan report rather than one being dropped quietly, and a full version's name no longer overrides the TV-size one's song details.
- 0.4.0.0: Full versions. Put the full-length song beside a theme as OP1-Full (video, audio or both; song details in the name work too) and it's kept with OP1: made playable like any theme, published as its own items ("Yuusha (Full)") in both libraries, and offered to clients (HasFullVersion, FullVideoMp4Url, FullAudioM4aUrl, and the full items' ids). Both libraries are republished once by themselves.
- 0.3.2.0: Fixes the Music Videos library showing one item per show: Jellyfin took videos named after their show's folder ("Show - OP1 - Song") for versions of one video. They're now named like the songs ("01 OP1 - Song"), and republished once by themselves.
- 0.3.1.0: Named Aster OP-ED in the plugin catalogue: Jellyfin names a plugin's folder after it, and refused "Aster OP/ED" (a folder name can't hold a slash), so 0.3.0.0 couldn't be installed from the repository. Nothing else changes.
- 0.3.0.0: OP/ED is now Aster OP/ED, one of the Aster companion plugins, installed from github.com/peppy6582/aster-companion-plugins. It updates in place: on first start it moves its settings and data (the theme index, playable copies, caches and published libraries' record) across from the old name. Nothing else changes; its API paths stay the same.
- 0.2.0.0: Publishes your themes as two Jellyfin libraries, kept up to date after every scan: a Music Videos library of the theme videos (links to the playable copies, with song, artists, show, season and episodes, a picture from the video, and Spoiler/NSFW tags; NSFW gets an adult rating for parental controls) and a Music library of their songs, an album per show with the show's art. Playlists, favourites and watched state then work as for anything else in Jellyfin. Turn it on and create both libraries from the Setup tab. For clients: themes now give their library items' ids, GET /OpEd/Library gives the libraries' ids, and GET /OpEd/LibraryItems/{id}/Theme gives the theme behind a library item.
- 0.1.4.0: A tidier settings page: Setup, Review and Library tabs. Clips are grouped by show, with Approve all and Reject all, keyboard shortcuts and previews on request. The library list can be searched and filtered, and a bar stays at the bottom while approved clips wait to be added to the library. New Rescan files button per show: replace a theme file, press it, and the plugin picks it up, makes it playable in the themes folder and moves the original to an _originals folder.
- 0.1.3.0: Works without Shokofin: AniList, MyAnimeList and Kitsu ids, then a title search (ten shows to a request, with an adjustable threshold), and seasons matched by premiere date. The editor says how each theme got its season and lets you type any AniDB id. Not-found shows are retried after 1, 3 and 7 days, then every 30. Duplicate AnimeThemes entries no longer override the main one, and themes now report overlap and whether a creditless version exists.
- 0.1.2.2: Same as 0.1.2.1 (settings page fix); re-released so the plugin repository lists it.
- 0.1.2.1: Fixes the settings page not loading in 0.1.2.0 (a script error).
- 0.1.2.0: Clearer wording throughout: settings page, plugin and task descriptions, and the README.
- 0.1.1.0: Looks themes up through the AnimeThemes GraphQL API with the user agent agreed with them. Season picker and OP/ED number on approval, library picker and a length hint for the chapter clip review queue, previews that stay put while clips are being cut, credit to AnimeThemes in the README and settings page.
- 0.1.0.0: First version. Indexes OP/ED theme files, matches them to shows and seasons, song details from AnimeThemes.moe, themes.json and file names, MP4/M4A copies for Apple TV, client API, and cutting missing OPs/EDs from episode chapters into a review queue.

name: Aster Aurora
description: Adds a rotating home hero banner, muted trailer backgrounds on details pages, card tilt and genre chips to jellyfin-web. Pairs with the Aurora custom CSS but works without it. Developed primarily with an AI coding assistant (Claude Code); see the README.
overview: Apple TV style behaviour for the Jellyfin web client.

versions.changelog: - 0.7.0.0: A button beside the sound button clears the page away so only the trailer or opening shows (Escape, a click or a scroll brings the page back). While a video plays it is shaded once, lightly, instead of three times (Jellyfin's backdrop dimmer and the skin's shade step aside). - 0.6.1.0: No more second Back arrow in the dashboard (on plugin pages and other pages under it): Aurora's Back button stays hidden wherever Jellyfin's header already has one. - 0.6.0.0: Anime show pages loop their opening behind the page instead of a trailer, as the Aster app does, from the Aster OP/ED plugin (the season you'd watch next, never a spoiler or NSFW one), with its name beside the sound button. The video gets the skin's shade, the sound button moves up under the header, and local trailers send the token Jellyfin 12 accepts (ApiKey). - 0.5.0.0: Matches the Aster skin and app: its colours carry into Aurora's elements, episode pages are titled with the episode's own name and an "S2, E2" line, a started title shows how much is left and resumes from the banner, and Home's header gets its backing back once the page scrolls. - 0.4.0.0: Now Aster Aurora, installed from the Aster companion plugins repository. Same plugin id, so it updates in place, and your Aurora settings move across on first start. - 0.3.1.0: Back button in the top-left corner. - 0.3.0.0: No flashes: custom CSS applied from the first frame, banner placeholder, pre-paint genre chips, art-less layout keyed off the page, reserved badge space. - 0.2.2.0: Also hide the stock Next Up block before first paint; never touch non-show pages. - 0.2.1.0: No more flash of the stock season cards before the Episodes row loads. - 0.2.0.0: Up Next style rows, quality badges, Episodes row with season tabs. - 0.1.0.0: First version. name: Aster Discovery and Tracking
description: Aster Media Player's tracking plugin. Each person links their own Trakt, Simkl, AniList, MyAnimeList, Last.fm, ListenBrainz and Hardcover accounts, and what they play is scrobbled there from any app; Aster also shows those services' lists for discovery. It's also where requests are turned on: Aster's Seerr features stay off unless they're enabled here, with the Seerr server's address.
overview: Discovery and tracking for Aster Media Player: each person's Discover page, scrobbling to their own accounts, and requests through Seerr.

versions.changelog:
- 0.9.8.0: Add to Watchlist: the apps can put a title on the person's Simkl Plan to Watch, and take it off again
  (POST and DELETE /AsterTracking/Watchlist/simkl, and GET /AsterTracking/Watchlist for where a title stands).
  Features lists the watchlists the apps can add to. Their Discover page picks up the change.
- 0.9.7.0: Aster's own apps on Simkl, AniList, MyAnimeList, Hardcover and Last.fm come from the release build, not the
  source; a build from the source uses Developer apps. Nothing changes for linked accounts.
- 0.9.6.0: Renamed Aster Discovery and Tracking (routes, settings and saved accounts unchanged). - 0.9.5.0: The server's rows check titles against Seerr's genres and keywords too, as Seerr's pages are, so a title
  blocked by a TMDB keyword (The Great Jahy, Ecchi) is out of the rows as well as its page.
- 0.9.4.0: Fixes 0.9.3 breaking Seerr's Discover rows (500) when genre or tag blocks are set. - 0.9.3.0: Seerr's lists and search are checked against each title's genres and keywords too (looked up from
  Seerr, kept a day), so a blocked title no longer shows as a card that won't open.
- 0.9.2.0: Blocks hold whichever service lists a title: duplicates share their genres and tags, anime without
  them (Simkl's) get AniList's, and films and shows without them get TMDB's.
- 0.9.1.0: Extra Discover blocks for several people at once: tick everyone they apply to. - 0.9.0.0: The admin can keep titles out of Discover: adult titles, and blocked genres and tags (AniList and
  MyAnimeList genres and tags, TMDB genres and keywords, the library's), for everyone and for particular people.
  Applied to the server's rows and to Seerr's lists, search and title pages passing through.
- 0.8.1.0: Faster Discover. Titles are matched to the library from an index kept in memory (a list went from
  about 3 s to milliseconds), a list's ids are filled once, and each person's Discover page is rebuilt in the
  background so it comes back at once.
- 0.8.0.0: Seerr through the server. The apps no longer sign in to Seerr: they call Seerr's API through the plugin
  (/AsterTracking/Seerr/api/v1/...), which calls Seerr as each person with its API key, so Seerr's permissions
  still apply. People without a Seerr account are imported from Jellyfin on first use. Requests needs Seerr's
  address and API key on this page.
- 0.7.0.0: Discover built on the server. GET /AsterTracking/Discover/Home sends each person their whole Discover
  page: Recommended for You (from what they watch here, their favourites and their services), Because You Watched,
  On Your Server Not Yet Watched, their watchlists, trending and this season's anime.
- 0.6.0.0: Discovery. The apps can show each person's Simkl, AniList and MyAnimeList lists (watchlists,
  watching, recommendations, trending, this anime season) in one shape, with TMDB ids (anime through ARM) and the
  title on this server when it's here.
- 0.5.0.0: ListenBrainz and Hardcover. ListenBrainz takes the songs people play (linked by pasting their user
  token), with MusicBrainz ids; Hardcover follows audiobook progress (linked with a code at hardcover.app):
  Currently Reading while listening, progress every 15 minutes and on stopping, and Read at the end.
- 0.4.0.0: Last.fm. People link it on the dashboard by approving Aster at last.fm (no code to copy); songs they play
  in any app show as now playing and are scrobbled once played half way or four minutes (longer than 30 seconds).
- 0.3.0.0: AniList and MyAnimeList. People link them on the dashboard (sign in, then paste the code shown), and
  each anime episode they watch moves that season's progress on (Watching, or Completed at the last episode); Shokofin
  seasons are matched through their AniDB ids and the ARM id map. AniDB ids from other plugins no longer count as
  anime for Simkl. Tokens about to run out are refreshed in the background.
- 0.2.0.0: Simkl. Each person links their Simkl account (a code entered at simkl.com/pin, from Aster's settings or
  the dashboard), and films and episodes they watch in any app are added to their Simkl history once stopped past
  85% or marked played; anime from Shokofin goes by its season's AniDB id. Sends that fail while Simkl is down are
  retried.
- 0.1.0.0: First release: the switch for Aster's requests. A Requests (Seerr) setting with Seerr's address, which
  the apps read before showing their Seerr features. Tracking services follow in the next releases.
